# Metaplate v0.6.0

Metaplate 0.6 turns image verification into a consistent SVG, PNG, JPEG, and WebP release gate while tightening the structural guarantees introduced in 0.5.

> **Upgrade recommendation:** Recommended for every 0.5 user. Next 15 users and callers using Resvg `crop` or dimension-changing `fitTo` settings must review the breaking changes below.

## Why upgrade

The 0.5 verifier reliably caught truncation but still accepted several specification-invalid headers and container layouts. Version 0.6 closes those false-positive build checks, adds SVG verification, improves CLI discoverability and font-language support, and promotes a real Next static export into packed-package verification.

The release also turns social metadata from a one-image shortcut into a configurable Open Graph/X model, adds honest target-aware compatibility diagnostics, and proves the packed package through real Astro and Express integrations.

## Highlights

### One verifier for SVG and raster output

- `metaplate verify` and `metaplate/image` now verify SVG dimensions and root structure in addition to PNG, JPEG, and WebP.
- SVG handling uses a conservative non-expanding parser boundary: unsafe declarations, malformed roots, and missing or non-positive pixel dimensions are rejected.
- `--format svg` lets SVG-only `createSvgOg` builds use the same check as raster pipelines.

### Stronger container guarantees

- PNG now enforces valid IHDR color/depth combinations, compression/filter/interlace methods, palette requirements and ordering, zlib window limits, and known critical chunks.
- WebP now enforces extended-canvas area, animation controls and frame bounds, zero RIFF padding, and VP8 first-partition bounds at the top level and inside VP8X/ANMF.
- JPEG now rejects zero-sized frame headers.
- The hardened replay rejects all 15 malformed containers from the 0.5 audit while preserving every real fixture and legal edge case.

### Better package ergonomics

- `npm install metaplate` now supplies React, Satori, and Resvg automatically;
  users no longer have to identify and install renderer packages themselves.
  Next remains application-supplied and optional.
- Package fonts preserve the optional BCP 47 `lang` tag used by Satori font selection.
- `metaplate --help` and `metaplate --version` are successful discovery commands.
- Packed-package verification first proves the one-command npm install against
  the registry, then performs a network-free real Next static export with
  lockfile-verified local peers and checks its generated Open Graph image and metadata.
- Framework recipes now link directly to the matching official Next.js, Astro,
  React Router, SvelteKit, and Express contracts, with Metaplate's tested
  runtime boundary alongside each link.
- Versioned, highlights-first release notes are now validated locally and in the publish workflow, with a draft-release workflow ensuring the GitHub release is reviewable before publication.

### Configurable social delivery

- Open Graph can carry ordered landscape, square, and fallback image descriptors while X uses an independent image when needed.
- X Cards support `summary` and `summary_large_image`, plus site/creator names and IDs.
- X-first `XCard` and `XImageOptions` types accompany the protocol-compatible
  Twitter aliases, and the README maps Open Graph/X channels to their platform
  consumers.
- The old one-image call remains the default and source-compatible; channel overrides are copied into independent descriptors.
- `socialImageCompatibility` reports universal and platform-specific URL, format, dimension, and file-size problems without inventing Discord or Instagram metadata contracts.

### Framework and runtime confidence

- `handlerFrom` derives copy from sync or async Astro, SvelteKit, React Router/Remix-style, and Next route arguments while preserving the fixed-copy `handler` API.
- Packed-package verification now builds Astro 7 metadata and a static image endpoint, serves a real Express 5 route, and type-generates, typechecks, builds, and fetches a React Router 7 resource route.
- The certified React Router 7 fixture now uses Vite 7.3.6 and fails if Vite's
  deprecated `envFile` warning returns.
- The runtime matrix distinguishes Node-compatible adapters from edge environments where native Resvg is unsupported.
- Dynamic-route guidance covers bounded copy, caching, concurrency/timeouts, and allowlisted remote assets.

## Breaking changes

- Satori, Resvg, and React are now required peer dependencies, so npm installs
  the complete renderer stack with Metaplate. This deliberately increases the
  footprint of metadata-only installs in exchange for a one-command setup.
- `metaplate/next` now supports the audited and release-tested Next `>=16.3.2 <17` line. Next 15 is no longer claimed because its remaining transitive advisories fail the release security gate.
- Resvg `crop` and dimension-changing `fitTo` settings now fail at plate creation. Define the intended output through the plate's `size` so rendered bytes and metadata cannot disagree.

## Install or upgrade

```sh
npm install metaplate@0.6.0
```

That single command includes the framework-neutral SVG and PNG renderer. Next
applications continue to supply their own compatible `next` dependency.

## Verification

- `npm run check` passes lint, source and example type checks, 236 tests, build, and a 29-file package dry run.
- `npm run check:package` passes against the exact local tarball, including standalone declaration consumers, offline Next static export, Astro static build, Express HTTP route, and React Router resource route.
- The malformed-input replay rejects 15 of 15 invalid containers and 316 of 316 truncation samples.
- npm registry signature/provenance verification remains a post-publication check and is not claimed here.
